libraries.name: Rapier (JS/WASM bindings)
libraries.what: Fast, deterministic 3D (and 2D) rigid-body physics engine written in Rust and compiled to WebAssembly.
libraries.good_for: Default 3D physics for a three.js game: rigid bodies, colliders, joints, raycasts, built-in kinematic character controller, vehicles.
libraries.not_for: Soft bodies, cloth or fluids; projects that cannot load WASM.
libraries.size_note: approx 2 MB min / 0.7 MB gz (the -compat build inlines the WASM as base64)
libraries.notes: The old dimforge/rapier.js repo is archived; the JS bindings now live in dimforge/rapier under typescript/. Use @dimforge/rapier2d-compat for 2D. Call `await RAPIER.init()` before creating a world.

libraries.name: cannon-es
libraries.what: Lightweight pure-JavaScript 3D rigid-body physics engine (maintained fork of cannon.js).
libraries.good_for: Simple 3D physics with no WASM: boxes, spheres, ragdolls, a basic raycast vehicle.
libraries.not_for: Large or stacked scenes, precise character controllers; new projects that can use Rapier.
libraries.notes: No commits since Jan 2024: stable and widely used, but effectively finished/unmaintained. Prefer Rapier for new games.

libraries.name: JoltPhysics.js
libraries.what: Emscripten/WASM port of Jolt, the AAA physics engine used in Horizon Forbidden West.
libraries.good_for: Heavy 3D physics: many bodies, vehicles (wheeled and tracked), character controllers, soft bodies.
libraries.not_for: Beginners wanting a small, idiomatic JS API (the API mirrors C++ and needs manual memory cleanup with Jolt.destroy).
libraries.size_note: wasm approx 1.5-3 MB depending on build flavour

libraries.name: Matter.js
libraries.what: Popular pure-JavaScript 2D rigid-body physics engine.
libraries.good_for: 2D physics toys and puzzle games (stacking, ragdolls, Angry-Birds-style); built into Phaser as 'Matter physics'.
libraries.not_for: 3D; very fast objects (tunnelling) or physics that must be deterministic across machines.

libraries.name: Planck.js
libraries.what: JavaScript rewrite of Box2D, the classic 2D physics engine.
libraries.good_for: 2D games that want Box2D behaviour: platformers, vehicles with joints, stable stacking.

libraries.name: three-avbd
libraries.what: GPU rigid-body physics (Augmented Vertex Block Descent, SIGGRAPH 2025) for three.js running on WebGPU compute.
libraries.good_for: Thousands of stacked/colliding bodies, destruction and voxel debris on WebGPU; see the companion three-voxel-destruction demo.
libraries.not_for: The WebGL2 starter (needs WebGPURenderer and a hardware WebGPU adapter; no WebGL fallback); mobile reach.
libraries.size_note: approx tens of KB gz (TypeScript + WGSL); untested estimate
libraries.notes: WebGPU-only, peer three >=0.186, young (0.3.x). sbobyn/three-voxel-destruction (MIT) is a Teardown-style demo built on it.

libraries.name: three-mesh-bvh
libraries.what: Builds a bounding-volume hierarchy for three.js meshes so raycasts and shape queries are orders of magnitude faster.
libraries.good_for: Fast mouse picking, character-vs-level collision against a static mesh (capsule queries), line of sight, decals on big meshes.
libraries.not_for: Full rigid-body dynamics (pair it with or use Rapier instead).
libraries.notes: Peer three >=0.159; CPU features work with any renderer, extra WebGPU compute examples exist.

libraries.name: three-bvh-csg
libraries.what: Fast boolean operations (union, subtract, intersect) on three.js meshes, built on three-mesh-bvh.
libraries.good_for: Cutting holes, carving terrain or walls at runtime, building level geometry procedurally.
libraries.not_for: Per-frame booleans on very dense meshes; non-manifold (open) geometry.
libraries.notes: Version 0.0.x (API may change); peer three >=0.179.

libraries.name: recast-navigation-js
libraries.what: WebAssembly port of Recast/Detour: builds navigation meshes from level geometry and moves agents along them.
libraries.good_for: NPCs that walk around a 3D level, crowds with avoidance, dynamic obstacles; three.js helpers in @recast-navigation/three.
libraries.not_for: Tile/grid games (use rot.js or a simple A*); flying agents.

libraries.name: navcat
libraries.what: Pure-JavaScript navigation mesh generation and querying for 3D floor-based navigation (no WASM).
libraries.good_for: Navmesh pathfinding when you want plain JS that agents can read and debug; same author as recast-navigation-js.
libraries.not_for: Projects needing a battle-tested 1.0 API (it is 0.x).

libraries.name: three-pathfinding
libraries.what: Small A* pathfinding over a navmesh that you model yourself (e.g. a simplified floor mesh exported from Blender).
libraries.good_for: Simple click-to-move or NPC routes on a hand-made navmesh, tiny bundle.
libraries.not_for: Generating navmeshes from level geometry, crowds or avoidance (use recast-navigation-js).

libraries.name: Yuka
libraries.what: Game AI toolkit: steering behaviours, state machines, goal-driven agents, perception, fuzzy logic and graph search.
libraries.good_for: Enemy and creature behaviour: seek/flee/wander/flocking, patrol-chase-attack state machines, vision cones.
libraries.not_for: Navmesh generation (pair with recast-navigation-js); machine learning.
libraries.notes: Last npm release 0.7.8 is old but the API is stable; renderer-agnostic, examples use three.js.

libraries.name: rot.js
libraries.what: Roguelike toolkit: grid A* and Dijkstra, field of view, dungeon/cave/maze generators, turn scheduler, seeded RNG.
libraries.good_for: Grid and tile games: roguelikes, tactics, dungeon layouts that you then render in 2D canvas or three.js.
libraries.not_for: Free 3D movement on arbitrary meshes.
libraries.notes: Stable and finished; infrequent commits.

libraries.name: MediaPipe Tasks Vision
libraries.what: Google's in-browser ML for webcam input: hand landmarks, gestures, face mesh, pose, segmentation.
libraries.good_for: Webcam-controlled games (hand tracking, gesture input, head/face control) that run fully on-device.
libraries.not_for: Low-end phones at high frame rates; games that must work without a camera permission.
libraries.size_note: approx 100 KB js + wasm approx 9-10 MB + model file 3-8 MB per task (load from CDN, cache)
libraries.notes: Category 'ai' here means machine-learning input, not NPC AI. Model files have their own model cards; check each before shipping.

libraries.name: camera-controls
libraries.what: Drop-in replacement for OrbitControls with smooth, animatable transitions (dolly, truck, fitToBox, setLookAt).
libraries.good_for: Smooth orbit/inspect cameras, cinematic moves between points, editor-style views, collision-aware boom.
libraries.not_for: First-person or tight third-person action cameras (write a custom follow camera).
libraries.notes: Call CameraControls.install({ THREE }) once before use.

libraries.name: Theatre.js
libraries.what: Timeline/keyframe animation library with a visual in-browser editor for sequencing cameras and objects.
libraries.good_for: Cutscenes, intros and scripted camera moves keyframed by hand, then played back with @theatre/core.
libraries.not_for: Gameplay animation driven by code; shipping the studio editor in a closed product.
libraries.size_note: core approx 60 KB gz; studio approx 1 MB (dev only)
libraries.notes: Licence caveat: @theatre/studio is AGPL-3.0, so only use it during development and ship @theatre/core alone. No commits since Aug 2024: treat as unmaintained.

libraries.name: GSAP
libraries.license: GSAP Standard 'no charge' license (proprietary, not OSI)
libraries.what: Very popular tweening/timeline animation library for any JS value, DOM, SVG or three.js object.
libraries.good_for: UI and menu animation, juice (squash, shake, pop), sequenced camera moves via timelines; all plugins now free.
libraries.not_for: Projects that need an OSI open-source licence, or building a no-code visual animation tool.
libraries.notes: Free incl. commercial use since 2025 (Webflow), under https://gsap.com/standard-license, not MIT. Condition: you may not use GSAP in 'tools that allow users to build visual animations without code' that compete with Webflow's animation tools without Webflow's written consent. Using GSAP inside a game is fine; GSAP's FAQ says AI-generated GSAP code is not a prohibited use.

libraries.name: tween.js
libraries.what: Tiny tweening engine with easing functions; the one used in many three.js examples.
libraries.good_for: Simple MIT-licensed tweens: door opening, pickups bobbing, camera easing.
libraries.not_for: Complex sequenced timelines (GSAP is richer).
libraries.notes: GitHub reports NOASSERTION; the LICENSE file is MIT (Penner easing equations credited).

libraries.name: three.quarks
libraries.what: General-purpose particle/VFX system for three.js with emitters, behaviours, trails and batched rendering.
libraries.good_for: Explosions, fire, smoke, magic, muzzle flashes, trails; effects can be designed in the quarks.art editor and loaded as JSON.
libraries.not_for: Fluid simulation; WebGPU-only projects (WebGPU rendering is still on its roadmap).
libraries.notes: Peer three >=0.182 (fine with 0.187).

libraries.name: postprocessing (pmndrs)
libraries.what: Efficient post-processing pipeline for three.js that merges effects into few passes (bloom, SMAA, DOF, tone mapping, vignette, etc.).
libraries.good_for: Adding bloom, colour grading, outlines, chromatic aberration and anti-aliasing cheaply.
libraries.not_for: WebGPURenderer (v6 is WebGL only; use three's TSL post nodes there).
libraries.notes: Peer three >=0.168 <0.188: OK for 0.187, but upgrading three past 0.187 needs a matching postprocessing release.

libraries.name: N8AO
libraries.what: High-quality, temporally stable screen-space ambient occlusion pass for three.js.
libraries.good_for: Grounding objects and adding contact shadows/depth to stylised or realistic scenes; works with three's EffectComposer or pmndrs postprocessing.
libraries.not_for: Low-end mobile at full resolution (use half-res mode); WebGPURenderer.
libraries.notes: GitHub says CC0-1.0, the npm package.json says ISC; both are permissive.

libraries.name: troika-three-text
libraries.what: Crisp SDF text rendered in 3D, generated on the fly from .ttf/.otf/.woff fonts.
libraries.good_for: Damage numbers, signs, labels and nameplates in the 3D world; any language/script with proper shaping.
libraries.not_for: Menus and HUD (plain HTML/CSS overlay is easier); WebGPURenderer.
libraries.size_note: approx 40 KB gz plus font files

libraries.name: lil-gui
libraries.what: Tiny floating panel of sliders, colour pickers and toggles bound to JS values (dat.gui replacement, used by three.js examples).
libraries.good_for: Live-tuning game feel (speeds, gravity, colours, camera offsets) during development.
libraries.not_for: Player-facing game menus.
libraries.notes: Stable/finished; infrequent commits.

libraries.name: Tweakpane
libraries.what: Compact tuning GUI with folders, tabs, graphs/monitors, point pickers and plugins.
libraries.good_for: Richer debug panels than lil-gui: FPS graphs, monitoring values, preset export/import.
libraries.not_for: Player-facing game menus.

libraries.name: nipplejs
libraries.what: Virtual on-screen joystick for touch devices.
libraries.good_for: Making a keyboard game playable on phones: movement stick plus look stick, dynamic or fixed position.
libraries.not_for: Desktop-only games; gamepads (use the browser Gamepad API).

libraries.name: stats-gl
libraries.what: FPS/CPU/GPU-time overlay for three.js that measures real GPU time via timer queries.
libraries.good_for: Finding out whether a slowdown is CPU or GPU bound while tuning performance.
libraries.not_for: Shipping to players (debug only).
libraries.notes: GitHub shows no LICENSE file; package.json declares MIT.

libraries.name: howler.js
libraries.what: Simple, reliable audio playback (Web Audio with HTML5 fallback): sprites, looping, fades, 3D/spatial sound.
libraries.good_for: Playing music and sound effects from files, audio sprites, unlocking audio on mobile.
libraries.not_for: Synthesising sounds or music in code (use ZzFX or Tone.js).
libraries.notes: Stable/finished; last release 2.2.4.

libraries.name: Tone.js
libraries.what: Web Audio framework for synths, effects, sequencing and musical timing.
libraries.good_for: Procedural or adaptive music, rhythm games, synthesized ambience and stingers.
libraries.not_for: Just playing a few audio files (howler is simpler and smaller).

libraries.name: ZzFX
libraries.what: Tiny sound-effect synthesizer: each sound is a short array of numbers, designed in a web sound designer.
libraries.good_for: Instant retro/arcade SFX (jumps, hits, coins, lasers) with zero audio files; easy for agents to generate.
libraries.not_for: Realistic or recorded sound.

libraries.name: ZzFXM
libraries.what: Tiny tracker-style music generator built on ZzFX.
libraries.good_for: Chiptune background music with no audio files, game-jam size limits.
libraries.not_for: Realistic or orchestral music.
libraries.notes: Finished/stable rather than actively maintained; copy the source file in (not on npm).

libraries.name: jsfxr
libraries.what: JavaScript port of sfxr, the classic retro sound-effect generator, with a web editor.
libraries.good_for: Retro SFX from presets (pickup, explosion, power-up) rendered at runtime or exported to WAV.
libraries.not_for: Music; realistic sound.
libraries.notes: Public domain (Unlicense).

libraries.name: simplex-noise
libraries.what: Fast 2D/3D/4D simplex noise for JavaScript, seedable with any PRNG.
libraries.good_for: Terrain heightmaps, wind, camera shake, wandering motion, procedural textures on the CPU.
libraries.not_for: Noise inside shaders (write GLSL/TSL noise instead).
libraries.notes: Stable/finished (v4).

libraries.name: seedrandom
libraries.what: Seeded pseudo-random number generators (Alea, xor4096 and others) for repeatable randomness.
libraries.good_for: Daily-seed levels, reproducible procedural worlds, replays and bug reproduction.
libraries.not_for: Cryptography.
libraries.notes: GitHub shows no LICENSE file; package.json and README state MIT. Stable/finished. A 10-line mulberry32 function is an alternative with no dependency.

libraries.name: Phaser
libraries.what: The most popular full-featured 2D HTML5 game framework: scenes, sprites, tilemaps, arcade and Matter physics, input, audio.
libraries.good_for: Any 2D game (platformer, shooter, puzzle, top-down RPG) with lots of examples and tutorials.
libraries.not_for: 3D; the three.js starter (it is a separate engine, not a three add-on).
libraries.notes: Phaser 4 is current; many online tutorials still target Phaser 3 APIs.

libraries.name: PixiJS
libraries.what: Fast 2D rendering engine (WebGL/WebGPU) for sprites, text, filters and graphics.
libraries.good_for: 2D games that want a fast renderer and their own game loop; pair with @pixi/sound, matter-js or planck.
libraries.not_for: People wanting a batteries-included engine (physics, scenes, tilemaps): use Phaser/Kaplay/Excalibur.
libraries.size_note: approx 150-200 KB gz full, tree-shakable in v8
libraries.notes: v8 renders with WebGL or WebGPU. @pixi/sound (MIT) is the matching audio library.

libraries.name: KAPLAY
libraries.what: Beginner-friendly 2D game library (successor to Kaboom.js) with a component-based API.
libraries.good_for: Quick, readable 2D games and jams; very approachable code for non-programmers.
libraries.not_for: 3D; very large or performance-heavy 2D games.

libraries.name: Excalibur
libraries.what: TypeScript-first 2D game engine with scenes, actors, collisions, tilemaps and Tiled support.
libraries.good_for: Structured 2D games in TypeScript; reached 1.0 so the API is stable.

libraries.name: LittleJS
libraries.what: Tiny, fast, dependency-free HTML5 game engine with rendering, physics, particles, input, audio (ZzFX) and tile layers.
libraries.good_for: Small 2D arcade games and jams; huge sprite counts; whole engine fits in an agent's context.
libraries.not_for: Complex 3D (it has only basic 3D support).

libraries.name: drei
libraries.what: Large collection of helpers (controls, loaders, text, environment, shaders) for React Three Fiber.
libraries.good_for: Projects already using React + @react-three/fiber.
libraries.not_for: The vanilla three.js starter: needs React and R3F. For vanilla three, look at @pmndrs/vanilla (drei-vanilla) or three/addons.
libraries.size_note: tree-shakable; React + R3F add approx 150 KB gz
libraries.notes: REACT ONLY. Same applies to @react-three/rapier, ecctrl, uikit and react-postprocessing.

libraries.name: Babylon.js
libraries.what: Full 3D game engine (alternative to three.js) with physics (Havok), GUI, audio, inspector and node material editor.
libraries.good_for: Starting a 3D game on a batteries-included engine instead of three.js.
libraries.not_for: Mixing into the three.js starter (it replaces three, it is not an add-on).
libraries.size_note: approx 1 MB+ gz full; tree-shakable ES modules
libraries.notes: Havok physics plugin (@babylonjs/havok) is MIT.

libraries.name: PlayCanvas Engine
libraries.what: Open-source 3D game engine (WebGL2/WebGPU) with entity-component system, physics integration and Gaussian splat support.
libraries.good_for: An alternative 3D engine with a game-oriented structure; the engine is usable without the hosted editor.
libraries.not_for: Mixing into the three.js starter (separate engine).
libraries.notes: The engine is MIT; the hosted PlayCanvas Editor is a separate commercial service.

libraries.name: InstancedMesh2 (@three.ez/instanced-mesh)
libraries.what: Enhanced three.js InstancedMesh with per-instance frustum culling, BVH raycasting, sorting, visibility, LOD and skinning.
libraries.good_for: Forests, grass clumps, crowds, bullets, asteroid fields: thousands of copies of a mesh at good FPS.
libraries.not_for: A handful of objects (plain meshes are simpler).

libraries.name: three-custom-shader-material (CSM)
libraries.what: Extends three's built-in materials (Standard, Physical, Toon...) with your own vertex/fragment shader code while keeping lighting and shadows.
libraries.good_for: Wind-swaying grass and trees, dissolve effects, vertex wobble, stylised shading without rewriting lighting.
libraries.not_for: WebGPURenderer/TSL (use node materials there).

libraries.name: glTF Transform
libraries.what: SDK and CLI for reading, editing and optimising glTF/GLB files (dedup, prune, resize/compress textures, Draco/meshopt, KTX2).
libraries.good_for: Shrinking AI-generated or downloaded models before shipping: `npx @gltf-transform/cli optimize in.glb out.glb`.
libraries.not_for: Runtime use in the game (it is a build-time tool).
libraries.size_note: build-time CLI/Node tool; not shipped to players

libraries.name: meshoptimizer / gltfpack
libraries.what: Mesh optimisation library plus gltfpack, a CLI that simplifies and compresses glTF files (EXT_meshopt_compression).
libraries.good_for: Making models much smaller and faster: simplification/LODs, quantisation, meshopt compression decoded by three's MeshoptDecoder.
libraries.not_for: Editing scene structure (use glTF Transform).
libraries.size_note: build-time CLI; runtime decoder approx 5 KB gz (ships with three as MeshoptDecoder)
libraries.notes: npm `meshoptimizer` is the JS/WASM library (simplifier, decoder).

libraries.name: Draco
libraries.what: Google's geometry compression for meshes and point clouds, decoded in three.js by DRACOLoader.
libraries.good_for: Very small download size for detailed static meshes.
libraries.not_for: Animated/morph-heavy models or fast loading on weak devices (meshopt usually decodes faster).
libraries.size_note: decoder wasm approx 300 KB (ships with three in examples/jsm/libs/draco)

libraries.name: KTX-Software (toktx / ktx CLI)
libraries.license: Apache-2.0 (mostly; bundled third-party parts under other permissive licences listed in LICENSES/)
libraries.what: Khronos tools to make KTX2 GPU-compressed textures (Basis Universal ETC1S/UASTC) that three's KTX2Loader reads.
libraries.good_for: Cutting texture GPU memory and download size, especially on mobile.
libraries.not_for: Runtime use (build-time tool; runtime transcoder ships with three).
libraries.size_note: build-time CLI; runtime basis transcoder wasm approx 500 KB (ships with three)
libraries.notes: GitHub shows NOASSERTION; LICENSE.md declares Apache-2.0. The encoder itself is BinomialLLC/basis_universal (Apache-2.0); glTF Transform can call it for you.

libraries.name: EZ-Tree
libraries.what: Procedural tree generator for three.js with many parameters, presets and a web editor that exports GLB.
libraries.good_for: Forests and hero trees without modelling; varied species from seeds; export to GLB for reuse.
libraries.not_for: Low-poly/stylised art direction out of the box; huge forests without instancing.
libraries.size_note: approx 20 KB gz plus bark/leaf textures (estimate)
libraries.notes: Peer three >=0.167.

libraries.name: three-pinata
libraries.what: Real-time mesh fracturing (Voronoi) and plane slicing for three.js.
libraries.good_for: Breakable crates, walls and statues, sword slicing, shattering glass; combine fragments with Rapier.
libraries.not_for: Non-closed meshes; fracturing every frame on dense meshes.
libraries.notes: Repo root has no LICENSE file (so GitHub shows none); the published library folder lib/ has an MIT LICENSE and package.json says MIT. Peer three >=0.158.

libraries.name: threejs-procedural-animals
libraries.what: Fully procedural animals for three.js: SDF-sculpted, auto-rigged and skinned, with fur/feathers/scales and IK gaits.
libraries.good_for: Wildlife, pets and creatures that walk and act with no model files, textures or animation clips.
libraries.not_for: Specific licensed characters or stylised art that must match concept art exactly.
libraries.size_note: unknown; import single species to keep bundle small (estimate tens to hundreds of KB)
libraries.notes: README mentions `npm install procedural-animals` but the package was not on npm on 2026-11-14; install with `npm install github:majidmanzarpour/threejs-procedural-animals`. Peer three r160+. Young project.

libraries.name: Procedural Terrains
libraries.what: Terrain studio for three.js: tiles, infinite worlds, planet mode, volumetric clouds, water, and GLB export.
libraries.good_for: Designing a terrain in the studio and exporting GLB/heightmaps for your game; reading its framework-agnostic engine code.
libraries.not_for: Dropping straight into the starter: the npm package pins three ~0.185.1 (peer conflict with 0.187) and the studio UI is React.
libraries.size_note: unknown; studio is a full app, engine module smaller (estimate)
libraries.notes: Core MIT; plugin licences documented beside each plugin package.

libraries.name: Procedural Planets
libraries.what: Procedural planets, gas giants and stars for three.js with GPU terrain LOD, clouds, oceans and atmospheres, as objects you add to your scene.
libraries.good_for: Space games: flyable planets with LOD, a Studio app for designing them and exporting to code.
libraries.not_for: Flat-ground games.
libraries.size_note: unknown (estimate tens of KB gz plus shaders)
libraries.notes: Very new (0.5.x, few stars). Peer three >=0.160, WebGL2 only.

libraries.name: threejs-particle-fluids
libraries.what: GPU position-based-fluids library for three.js: liquids, soft bodies, cloth and smoke simulated on WebGPU.
libraries.good_for: Splashy water, goo, smoke and soft-body toys on WebGPU-capable desktops.
libraries.not_for: The WebGL2 starter: WebGPU only (no fallback) and peer three pinned to >=0.184 <0.185.
libraries.notes: Bundled demo models are CC0 (Kenney, Poly Haven); see THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md. Same author's threejs-fire-pro (MIT) is also WebGPU-only and pins three 0.185.1.

libraries.name: Ultra-Water
libraries.what: Real-time FFT ocean renderer for three.js (WebGL2) with shore breakers, foam, caustics, underwater view and buoyancy.
libraries.good_for: Sea, island and boat games; reference for a buoyancy model and shoreline waves.
libraries.not_for: Low-end mobile at full quality (it has a phone profile, but is GPU heavy); a drop-in npm package (copy the modules from the repo).
libraries.size_note: demo app; water modules plus shaders, size unknown
libraries.notes: Code adapted from other projects is listed in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md; keep those notices if you copy code.

libraries.name: Ultra Elements
libraries.what: Lab of 39 tunable elemental spell effects for three.js (WebGL2) with a ground reaction field (scorch, frost, wet, acid).
libraries.good_for: Copying or studying spell/ability VFX for action and RPG games; tuning effects with live sliders.
libraries.not_for: A packaged library API (it is an app; lift the effect modules you need).
libraries.notes: See THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md for adapted code (e.g. the pool after Evan Wallace's WebGL Water).

libraries.name: Elemental Sandbox (LinearAbiltyCastingThreeJS)
libraries.what: Skillshot ability sandbox in three.js + GLSL: MOBA-style aim arrows and AoE circles with six spell effects.
libraries.good_for: Reference for ability targeting UX (line casts, ground-targeted AoE) and hand-written GLSL spell VFX.
libraries.not_for: A reusable library (it is a Vite app); WebGPURenderer.
libraries.notes: Repo name is misspelled ('Abilty'). Same author has other MIT three.js demos: BuildingGeneratorThreeJS, OceanThreejs, WaterThreeJS, RainSystemThreeJS, SnowSystemThreeJS, GrassSystemThreeJS (actually a soil/terrain studio), VegetationGeneratorThreeJS (WebGPU ivy), all built on three ~0.185.

libraries.name: Effekseer for WebGL
libraries.what: Web runtime for Effekseer, a free particle-effect editor used in many commercial games, with three.js integration.
libraries.good_for: Designing complex particle effects in the Effekseer desktop editor and playing them in a three.js game.
libraries.not_for: Effects authored purely in code (three.quarks fits better).
libraries.notes: Not on npm: download the release zip linked from the README. New version adds WebGPU alongside WebGL.

libraries.name: Eanpa Sky
libraries.what: Volumetric cloud sky, day/night cycle and weather system for three.js WebGPU (TSL) with earth and sci-fi skyboxes.
libraries.good_for: Open-world skies with weather on WebGPU desktops.
libraries.not_for: The WebGL2 starter: WebGPU required, and it vendors a locally patched three r186.
libraries.size_note: app with vendored three; size unknown
libraries.notes: Same author's SeedThree (MIT, WebGPU tree/plant generator) is another option. Do not confuse with their AGPL-3.0 eidoverse repos.

libraries.name: three-geospatial (takram)
libraries.what: Physically based atmosphere (precomputed scattering), volumetric clouds and effects for three.js, built for geospatial scenes.
libraries.good_for: Realistic sky, sun and aerial perspective; flight and open-world games; volumetric clouds via @takram/three-clouds.
libraries.not_for: Stylised skies; WebGPURenderer (released packages use WebGL with pmndrs postprocessing).
libraries.size_note: approx tens of KB gz code plus precomputed LUT textures (estimate)
libraries.notes: Packages are beta/alpha. React/R3F peers are optional; vanilla three works. Needs `postprocessing`.

libraries.name: pixel-plays
libraries.license: MIT (code only; music is not MIT, see MUSIC.md)
libraries.what: Collection of small browser games drawn as isometric pixel dioramas on a low-res canvas, no build step and no dependencies.
libraries.good_for: Reference for crisp pixel-art canvas scaling and compact single-file browser games.
libraries.not_for: Reusing its music (separate terms).
libraries.notes: Licence caveat: code is MIT but the music is not; read MUSIC.md before reusing any audio.

libraries.name: Godot Advanced Vehicle
libraries.what: Advanced raycast vehicle controller for Godot in GDScript (tyre model, drivetrain, differentials, suspension).
libraries.good_for: Porting a vehicle model to JS (e.g. onto Rapier or Jolt raycast vehicles).
libraries.not_for: Direct use in a browser game (GDScript, not JavaScript).
libraries.notes: Code MIT; bundled models and textures belong to their authors (see README links); engine sound sample is CC0.
